title: Game Math
body:
Goal: write functions that return their answer, so the game can use it.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. Look for the word None. Bug hunt: why does xp_needed show the number on its own line and then say None?
  2. TODO 1: change print(...) into return ....
  3. TODO 2 and 3: finish damage(): never less than 0, then return result.
  4. TODO 4: finish is_critical(). Tip: return roll >= 19 gives back True or False all by itself.
  5. TODO 5: remove the # from the two health lines and run again.

Done looks like:

To reach level 5 you need 500 XP.
The dragon attacks with 12 against your shield of 5: 7 damage!
The goblin attacks with 3 against your shield of 5: 0 damage.
Health left: 33
Roll 7: critical hit? False
Roll 19: critical hit? True
Roll 20: critical hit? True

Extra: write heal(health, potion) that returns the new health, but never more than 100.

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at xp_needed first. It shows a number on its own line, and then your message says None. Ask yourself what print does with an answer and what return does.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: print only shows something on the screen. return hands a value back to the code that called the function. For damage, use an if to fix a number below zero. For is_critical, a comparison like >= already gives True or False.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: xp_needed should hand its answer back instead of showing it. In damage, write if result < ____: and set result to a new number. Then hand result back. For is_critical, finish return roll >= ____.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Game Math
# Run this first and read what it prints. Something strange happens with
# xp_needed: it shows a number AND the word None. Why? (Bug hunt!)


def xp_needed(level):
    """Return how many experience points (XP) you need to reach this level."""
    # TODO 1: this function PRINTS the answer but does not hand it back.
    print(level * 100)


def damage(attack, shield):
    """Return the damage a hit does. The shield blocks some of the attack,
    but damage can never be less than 0."""
    result = attack - shield
    # TODO 2: if result is less than 0, make it 0.
    # TODO 3: hand result back with return.


def is_critical(roll):
    """Return True if a 20-sided dice roll is a critical hit (19 or 20)."""
    # TODO 4: return True for 19 or 20, otherwise False.
    return False


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(f"To reach level 5 you need {xp_needed(5)} XP.")
    hit = damage(12, 5)
    print(f"The dragon attacks with 12 against your shield of 5: {hit} damage!")
    blocked = damage(3, 5)
    print(f"The goblin attacks with 3 against your shield of 5: {blocked} damage.")
    # TODO 5: when TODO 3 is done, remove the # at the start of the next two lines.
    # health = 40 - hit - blocked
    # print(f"Health left: {health}")
    for roll in [7, 19, 20]:
        print(f"Roll {roll}: critical hit? {is_critical(roll)}")
